title: Prime-field tensor generators for constructible complexes
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, put $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), and let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian $\Lambda$-algebra. Work in the ordinary derived categories of module sheaves on the small etale site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For a commutative ring $R$, write $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ for complexes with bounded cohomology admitting a finite locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification] on each stratum of which (after restriction) each cohomology sheaf is locally constant of finite type [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules], i.e. locally constant with finitely generated $R$-module stalks [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; for $R=\Lambda$ this is [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. For a finitely generated $A$-module $N$, let $N_X$ be its constant module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The category $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ is exactly the smallest strictly full subcategory of $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ containing every object $$N_X\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}F,\qquad N\text{ a finitely generated }A\text{-module},\quad F\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda),$$ and closed under integer shifts, cones of morphisms between its objects, finite direct sums, and direct summands. The tensor is [def-kun-derived-tensor], with the $A$-action on $N_X$. The shifts, cones and summands are taken in the ordinary derived category with its usual triangulated structure [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 7.4.6 (finite filtration with direct-summand tensor quotients), p. 307, and Proposition 7.4.1 and its proof, pp. 305, 308

proof.text: Write $\mathcal T$ for the subcategory generated in the statement. First $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ is closed under the listed operations. The weak Serre assertion [lem-sfb-discrete-noetherian-constructible-serre] applies to $A$ without assuming its underlying set finite. Its affine-local notion equals the finite-global-stratification notion here by [lem-sfb-noetherian-global-constructibility]; over a Noetherian ring finite generation implies finite presentation by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation], and the converse follows from a finite presentation. In the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] of $K\to L\to C\to K[1]$, $H^q(C)$ is an extension of $\operatorname{coker}(H^q(K)\to H^q(L))$ by $\ker(H^{q+1}(K)\to H^{q+1}(L))$. Thus cones have constructible cohomology and a finite cohomology interval. Shifts and finite sums preserve both conditions. For a retract $P$ of $K$, $H^q(P)$ is the image of the idempotent on $H^q(K)$, hence the kernel of one minus that idempotent; it is constructible and vanishes wherever $H^q(K)$ does. This also proves closure under direct summands.

source.place: 7.4.1, the triangulated constructible ambient category, p. 305; explicit weak Serre verification from Stacks Tags 03RZ and 095E

proof.text: For a finitely generated $A$-module $N$, the functor $N_X\otimes_{\Lambda_X}-$ is exact. Indeed [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] and [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] identify its effect on a short exact sequence at every geometric point with tensoring a short exact sequence of $\Lambda$-vector spaces by $N$. Such a sequence splits by lifting a basis of its quotient, so tensoring is exact; stalk isomorphism detection [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks] then gives exactness on sheaves. It follows directly that the degree-zero sheaf $N_X$ is K-flat: tensoring any acyclic complex remains acyclic. Thus $N_X\otimes^L_\Lambda F$ has cohomology $N_X\otimes_\Lambda H^q(F)$. On a stratum and a cover where $H^q(F)$ is constant of finite $\Lambda$-dimension $d$, the basis gives a map from the constant $A$-module $N^{\oplus d}$ to this sheaf. It is an isomorphism on stalks: constants have their stated stalks by clause (1) of [lem-pod-lisse-tensor-and-scalar-extension], and the tensor stalk formula identifies the map with $N^{\oplus d}\cong N\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda^d$. Stalk detection makes it an isomorphism of sheaves. These are finite local models, and the cohomology interval is that of $F$. Every generator lies in $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, so Step 1 gives $\mathcal T\subseteq D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$.

source.place: 7.4.1, tensor functors in the prime-field case; explicit flatness and local-model verification

proof.text: Let $E$ be a constructible $A$-module sheaf. Apply [lem-per-constructible-finite-monodromy-filtration] to obtain its finite filtration with quotients $k_!L$ and the factorizations $k=j i$ supplied there. It suffices to put each such $k_!L$ in $\mathcal T$: each short exact sequence of the filtration gives a distinguished triangle by [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle], and induction on its finite length, starting with zero, then puts $E[0]$ in $\mathcal T$.

source.place: 7.4.2 and the first reduction of 7.4.6, pp. 305, 307

proof.text: Fix one such $S,L,c:Y\to S$, and put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_S(Y)$ and $B=\Lambda[G]$. This is a finite-dimensional $\Lambda$-algebra with basis the finite set $G$. By [lem-per-galois-cover-module-descent], $L=T_{c,A}(M)$ for an $A$-finite module $M$ with $A$-linear $G$-action. Regard $M$ as a module over $A\otimes_\Lambda B=A[G]$; its $A$-generators also generate over this algebra. Apply [lem-per-finite-algebra-external-tensor-filtration] to $M$. Exactness and additivity of $T_{c,A}$ turn its filtration into a filtration of $L$ whose quotients are retracts of $N_S\otimes_\Lambda L_0$, where $N$ is $A$-finite and $L_0=T_{c,\Lambda}(V)$ for a simple $B$-module $V$. Since $B$ is finite-dimensional, any nonzero $v\in V$ gives the surjection $B\to V$, $b\mapsto bv$; hence $V$ is finite-dimensional over $\Lambda$. The descent statement therefore makes $L_0$ a finite-type locally constant $\Lambda$-sheaf on $S$.

source.place: 7.4.6, finite group algebra reduction, and Lemma 7.4.7, pp. 307-308

proof.text: The functor $k_!=j_!i_*$ is exact. For $j_!$ this is [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. For the closed immersion $i$, [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] identifies each stalk of $i_*Q$ with the corresponding stalk of $Q$ on the closed subset and with zero elsewhere. Exactness of stalks and their detection of isomorphisms therefore give exactness of $i_*$; the same argument applies to module sheaves because kernels and cokernels have the induced coefficient actions. Consequently applying $k_!$ to the filtration in Step 4 preserves its short exact sequences and retract diagrams. Each resulting quotient is a retract of $k_!(N_S\otimes_\Lambda L_0)$.

source.place: 7.4.2 and 7.4.6, exact stratum extension by zero; Stacks Tags 03DJ, 03S5 and finite stalk formula

proof.text:
Put $F_0=k_!L_0$. On $S$ it restricts to $L_0$, and off $S$ it restricts to zero: for $j_!$ use [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks], and for $i_*$ use [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula]. Add to $S$ the closed complement of the chosen open $V$ and the open complement $V\setminus S$ in $V$; these give a finite locally closed stratification of $X$. Thus $F_0$ is a constructible $\Lambda$-sheaf. There is a natural comparison
$$N_X\otimes_\Lambda k_!L_0\longrightarrow k_!(N_S\otimes_\Lambda L_0).$$
Construct its closed factor by restriction of sections to $S$ followed by the tensor map, and its open factor on the extension-by-zero presheaves, then sheafify. By [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] and the two extension stalk formulas, this map is the identity on $N\otimes_\Lambda(L_0)_{\bar s}$ at a point of $S$ and the map $0\to0$ elsewhere. It is therefore an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks]. Step 2 identifies its left side with $N_X\otimes^L_\Lambda F_0$. This is one of the stated generators, so all quotients from Step 5 lie in $\mathcal T$ by closure under retracts.

source.place: 7.4.6, tensor quotients extended from strata; explicit mixed-coefficient stalk comparison

proof.text: Induct up the finite filtration of $k_!L$ in Step 5, using [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle] at each short exact sequence and closure of $\mathcal T$ under cones and shifts. Step 6 puts each quotient in $\mathcal T$, hence $k_!L\in\mathcal T$. The induction in Step 3 now gives $E[0]\in\mathcal T$ for every constructible $A$-module sheaf $E$. This includes the empty filtration and zero sheaf.

source.place: 7.4.6 and conclusion of the proof of 7.4.1, pp. 307-308

proof.text:
Finally take $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and choose $a\le b$ with $H^q(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], $\tau_{\le a-1}K$ is acyclic and $\tau_{\le b}K\to K$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For $a\le q\le b$, [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] gives
$$\tau_{\le q-1}K\longrightarrow\tau_{\le q}K\longrightarrow H^q(K)[-q]\longrightarrow(\tau_{\le q-1}K)[1].$$
Step 7 and shifts put the third term in $\mathcal T$. Starting from the zero object $\tau_{\le a-1}K$, induction on $q$ puts $\tau_{\le b}K$, hence $K$, in $\mathcal T$. Together with Step 2 this proves equality of the strictly full subcategories.

source.place: 7.4.1 and its final reduction to constructible sheaves, pp. 305, 308; Stacks Tag 08J5

proof_origin.place: Expose XVII, 7.4.2, 7.4.6, 7.4.7 and proof of 7.4.1, pp. 305-308, with explicit ordinary-derived and stalk calculations

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NK-62477650e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the mathematics in full against ILO XVII pp. 301-308 (7.2.1-7.2.7, 7.3.1-7.3.7, 7.4.1-7.4.7 and the proof of 7.4.1). The item is the ℓ-specialization of 7.4.1 with finitely generated N, which is no weaker; its statement is unchanged; X is an arbitrary Noetherian scheme and A an arbitrary Noetherian F_ℓ-algebra. All 8 steps check against the cited statements. Step 1: weak Serre closure for arbitrary Noetherian R, the global/affine-local comparison, cone cohomology from the long exact sequence, and summands via ker(1-e). Step 2: stalks of the tensor product and of a constant sheaf (clause 1 of lem-pod-lisse, arbitrary ring), exactness over a field, N_X is K-flat, local model N^d. Steps 4-6: the descent equivalence with B=F_ℓ[G] and A⊗B=A[G]; the mixed tensor clause carries the diagonal G-action; k_! is exact through the j_! node and the finite stalk formula for the closed immersion; the comparison N_X⊗k_!L_0≅k_!(N_S⊗L_0) checked on stalks. Step 8: truncation induction from the zero object. All three new nodes are true and are not item clauses or duplicates. The algebra node is 7.4.7; I tested A=F_ℓ, F_ℓ[G] with ℓ dividing |G|, and A=B=F_{ℓ^2}. The descent node holds for arbitrary R, A and N because Y is connected; the existing torsor-descent and cor-galois-lisse nodes need finite rings. The geometric filtration node stays true despite the ILO 7.2.7 warning, because its strata may be refined (nodal cubic with monodromy [[t,1],[1,0]]); generic trivialization, spreading out and Noetherian induction prove it. Batch 5: lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar and lem-pod-lisse-tensor-and-scalar-extension (clause 1) are generic sheaf algebra. Their closures (66 and 70 nodes) contain no trace-formula node, and their only sec-poincare-duality members are themselves and def-pod-ring-scalar-extension, so neither is a statement assumed by the PD or trace-formula leaves nor a step of their proofs: accepted. I accept all 14 declared tool_uses as generic black boxes. Form: proof_deps equal the union of the step uses, all steps are under 2000 characters, no SGA. Cosmetic only: Step 5 names two stalk nodes in words rather than in brackets. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem primeFieldTensor_devissage (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ)) A] : DerivedCategory.boundedConstructible (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X = (primeFieldTensorGenerators X ℓ A).triangEnvelope
lean.note: The generators are defined using all representative complexes and the sheafified sectionwise mixed tensor from def-pc-mixed-total-tensor. Over the prime field N_X is K-flat, so this computes the specified derived tensor with its A-action through N; no flatness hypothesis on N over A is imposed. The arbitrary-Noetherian-coefficient side uses the existing upstream DerivedCategory.boundedConstructible, whose finite-type stalk convention is Module.Finite, not finiteness of the coefficient ring. Both helper constructions and the named zero-morphism proof needed for mapping complexes are recorded in declarations.
